knowledge-base.overview: Language-specific guardrails and patterns for HTML and CSS. Loaded when agents work on .html, .htm, .css, .scss, or .less files. Applies to HTML5, CSS3, SCSS/LESS, responsive design, and WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility.

core-principles.principle: Use HTML elements for their meaning, not their appearance; style with CSS.
Every page must be navigable by keyboard, screen reader, and assistive technology.
Build a solid HTML foundation, then layer on CSS and JavaScript.
Design for the smallest viewport, then enhance with min-width media queries.
Minimize render-blocking resources; prefer system fonts, modern image formats, and critical CSS inlining.

guardrail.rule: Every img must have an alt attribute. Decorative images use alt="". Missing alt is a WCAG 2.1 Level A failure.
All form inputs must have associated label elements (for/id pairing or aria-label). Never use placeholder as a label substitute.
guardrail.good: We will never share your email.

guardrail.rule: Never use outline: none on interactive elements without providing a replacement focus indicator. Keyboard users depend on visible focus.
Use button for actions and a for navigation. Never use div onclick or span onclick for interactive elements.
Color contrast: 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text (18px+ bold or 24px+). Do not rely on color alone to convey information.
Headings must follow a logical outline. Never skip heading levels for styling purposes. Use h1-h6 to reflect document structure.
Never use !important outside utility class overrides. Fix specificity conflicts instead.
Max 3 levels of nesting in CSS (native or preprocessor). Deep nesting creates brittle specificity chains.
No inline styles unless dynamically computed by JavaScript. Style belongs in CSS files.
Use custom properties (CSS variables) for all theme values: colors, spacing, typography, border radii. Never hardcode theme values in component rules.
Animate only transform and opacity to avoid layout reflows and paint invalidation.
Set explicit width/height or aspect-ratio on media elements to prevent Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS).
Mobile-first: write base styles for small viewports, add complexity with min-width media queries. Use rem/em for sizing; reserve px for borders and fine details only.

rules.rule: Use main once per page; header, footer, nav, aside for landmarks
Use article for self-contained content; section for thematic groups with a heading
Use figure/figcaption for captioned media; time datetime="..." for dates
Use ul, ol, dl for groups of related items — not div sequences
Include a skip-to-content link as the first focusable element on every page

css-architecture.description: Use @layer for specificity control and predictable cascade. One component per file. BEM or utility-first — pick one and stay consistent.

pattern.name: Grid (2D) vs Flexbox (1D)
pattern.description: Use CSS Grid for page layouts with rows and columns; use Flexbox for single-axis alignment.

pattern.name: Container Queries
pattern.description: Component-level responsiveness based on parent container width, not viewport width.

pattern.name: The :has() Selector
Dark Mode and User Preferences
Fluid Typography
pattern.example: /* Scales between 1rem at 320px viewport and 1.5rem at 1440px */ .body-text { font-size: clamp(1rem, 0.5rem + 1.5vw, 1.5rem); }

pattern.name: Responsive Images
pattern.description: Use picture with format fallbacks. Set explicit dimensions to prevent layout shift.

category.name: Perceivable
category.item: All images have descriptive alt (or alt="" for decorative)
Color contrast: 4.5:1 body text, 3:1 large text
Information not conveyed by color alone
Text resizable to 200% without content loss
Captions for video; transcripts for audio

category.name: Operable
category.item: All functionality keyboard-accessible (Tab, Enter, Escape, arrows)
Logical focus order; visible focus indicators
No keyboard traps; modals return focus on close
Skip navigation link as first focusable element

category.name: Understandable
category.item: Form inputs have visible labels and descriptive error messages

category.name: Robust
category.item: ARIA roles, states, and properties match widget behavior
Tested with screen reader (VoiceOver, NVDA, or JAWS)

tooling.commands: npx stylelint "**/*.css" # CSS lint npx stylelint "**/*.css" --fix # CSS lint auto-fix npx htmlhint "**/*.html" # HTML validation npx prettier --check "**/*.{html,css,scss}" # Format check npx prettier --write "**/*.{html,css,scss}" # Format fix npx lighthouse http://localhost:3000 --output html --view # Performance audit npx @axe-core/cli http://localhost:3000 # Accessibility check npx pa11y http://localhost:3000 # Accessibility test

responsive-breakpoints.note: Also test with 200% browser zoom applied at each breakpoint.

quick-reference.item: ALWAYS — decorative: alt=""; informative: descriptive text
ALWAYS associate with for/id; never use placeholder as label
NEVER outline: none without replacement; keyboard users depend on it
button for actions; a for navigation; never div onclick
4.5:1 normal text; 3:1 large text (18px+ bold or 24px+)
Logical outline; never skip levels for styling
Only in utility classes; fix specificity instead
All theme values — colors, spacing, typography, radii
Only transform and opacity to avoid reflows
Base styles for small screens; min-width queries for larger
picture + srcset (avif/webp/jpg); explicit width/height; lazy loading
prefers-color-scheme media query + data-theme attribute toggle
reset, base, layout, components, utilities — prevents specificity wars
